verdict.reasoning: Doctor (patient) reports: "I've really dry, itchy skin" and localizes it to "All over my arms and my hands, mainly" and says it "started a few days ago."
Patient confirms timing with swimming: Patient: "I went swimming a few days ago." and, when asked "did your symptoms start after you went swimming?" replies "Yes."
When asked if it has spread to chest, legs, or face, the clinician says: "Has it spread to your chest, your legs, your face?" and then answers "No." indicating no spread.
Patient describes: "my skin's quite red" (erythematous), had already said it was "dry, itchy" (pruritic and dry), and also says "I don't have any spots."
Patient states: "I'm using coconut butter for the past few days." and when asked "So the coconut butter hadn't helped with the itch?" answers "No."
Patient says: "No fever. I'm not sweating either." and later, to "No fevers, no. Vomiting?" responds "No," and to "No problems with vomiting or loose stools?" responds "No."

Patient confirms: "Yeah, I've been drinking and eating as normal." and, to questions about bowels and urine, responds "Yeah" and "Yep" to "Are your bowels working okay?" and "your waterworks are all okay?"
When asked "Do you feel genuinely run down? Do you feel tired?" patient answers: "Yeah, I think I have been quite tired."
Clinician asks: "there's no problems of skin problems in the past, things like eczema or dermatitis?" and patient replies "No"; this includes denial of prior eczema.
Same exchange: "no problems of skin problems in the past, things like eczema or dermatitis?" and patient replies "No," denying past dermatitis.
Patient states: "I'm currently taking microgen." Clinician clarifies: "Microgynal?" and patient answers "Yeah." Clinician then explains it is a contraceptive pill.
In allergy discussion: "Do you suffer from allergies?..." patient answers: "I think I might be lactose intolerant." indicating lactose intolerance as an allergy/intolerance.
For family history: patient says, "Yeah, so my dad has asthma".
When asked "any skin problems I should be aware of?" regarding family, patient answers "No." indicating no family history of skin disease.
On social history: "Socially, who do you live with at home?" Patient: "It's just me." Clinician: "Live alone?" Patient: "Yep."
Employment: patient states "I work as a teacher." Later clinician specifies "you meant you work as a primary school teacher." and patient confirms "Yes, that's right."
Early in the consultation: "I've been really stressed at work for the past few days" and later discussion links this to work as a teacher.
When asked "do you smoke at all?" and "Are you a smoker?" patient replies "No, I don't smoke."
When asked "Do you drink much in the way of alcohol?" patient answers "No."

Clinician says: "I wonder whether you may have something called dermatitis" and summarizes: "dry, itchy rash on your... hands... and your arms, which started perhaps after swimming a few days ago, but no other symptoms. You're feeling otherwise? Well, no fevers, no bleeding or discharge from skin." This matches the described dermatitis without systemic symptoms.
Clinician: "we can readily treat it with a couple of options. We have steroid creams I can give you, which will help with inflammation" indicating a prescription of topical steroid cream.

Clinician: "and something called emollients. Which can help with the dry skin. And that's something you just need to kind of paste onto your skin throughout the day for the next few days"—i.e., liberal emollient use.
Clinician advises: "You can also try antihistamines, so you can get things over the counter. Pyritin, loratadine. That can sometimes help with the itchiness."
Clinician: "I can give you a patient information lethal [leaflet] about that, which gives a bit more information about the disease" referring to dermatitis.
Clinician explicitly states: "Paracetamol on this occasion wouldn't be helpful. Painkillers wouldn't be helpful on this occasion."

Clinician: "let's see how the next few days go. And if it's still not getting better, come back and see me next week and we can have another look again at your symptoms." This corresponds to follow up in about a week if not improving.
Rash description: "I've really dry, itchy skin" and "my skin's quite red" localized to "my arms and my hands, mainly"—pruritic, erythematous, and dry rash on hands and arms.

Patient says: "No fever. I'm not sweating either." and later, to "No fevers, no. Vomiting?" responds "No," and also denies problems with loose stools. This covers denial of fever, sweating, vomiting, and diarrhea.
Patient reports: "Yeah, I've been drinking and eating as normal." and confirms bowels and urine are okay: "Yeah" to bowels and "Yep" to waterworks.
To "Do you feel genuinely run down? Do you feel tired?" the patient answers "Yeah, I think I have been quite tired." indicating fatigue.
